packets.responsibility: Pure geometry layer for the tween-curve-strip feature: which frames on a layer are keyframes, which consecutive keyframe pairs actually have a generated tween between them, how much extra row height (if any) a layer's row needs to show its strip, and the row-height-aware pixel<->layer-index conversions (visualTopOfLayer/frameGridTotalRowsHeight/layerIndexAtGridY) that replace the old flat li*ROW_H arithmetic now that rows can have unequal heights.
behavior: Section header (4344) plus a long lead-in comment (4345-4356) records the feature's origin (was a thin 8px sparkline, became the same rich draggable-point editor as the floating popup per explicit request) and the non-overlap invariant: only layers with an actual tween span grow taller (TWEEN_ROW_EXTRA_H), others stay at plain ROW_H.

layerKeyframeList (4356-4361): reads state.layers[li]; returns [] if the layer is missing; otherwise scans ld.frames[0..state.totalFrames-1] and collects every frame index whose frame has isKeyframe truthy, in ascending order.

layerTweenSpans (4366-4377, preceded by an explanatory comment at 4362-4365 naming this the single definition of 'this layer has a tween to show'): calls layerKeyframeList(li); for each consecutive pair of keyframes [fA,fB], scans every frame strictly between them and marks hasTween true the moment any frame has isInterpolated truthy (first-match break, no further scanning of that pair); collects [fA,fB] into spans only when hasTween is true. A keyframe pair with a gap but no generated interpolated frame between them (e.g. two adjacent keyframes with fB===fA+1) is silently omitted from the result.
layerHasTweenSpans (4378): one-line boolean wrapper, `layerTweenSpans(li).length>0`.
TWEEN_ROW_EXTRA_H (4379): module-level constant, 92 (pixels) — the fixed extra height a qualifying row grows by.

layerCurveRowExtraHeight (4380-4382, with a one-line comment at 4380): returns 0 immediately if state.showTweenCurves is falsy (feature toggled off); otherwise returns TWEEN_ROW_EXTRA_H if layerHasTweenSpans(li) else 0. This is the single decision point both the row-height formula below and renderTimeline's own row-building loop (outside this packet, C19m-owned, lines 4270-4300) must agree on for the two to never desync.

frameGridRowHeight (4392, preceded by a five-line comment at 4383-4391 naming it the single source of truth for a layer's current total row height): `ROW_H+layerCurveRowExtraHeight(li)` — reads the app.js-owned global ROW_H constant (=34) and adds the per-layer extra from above. Reduces to plain ROW_H whenever the toggle is off or the layer has no tween span.

visualTopOfLayer (4401-4404, preceded by an eight-line comment at 4393-4400 explaining why a flat li*ROW_H formula no longer holds): sums frameGridRowHeight(li2) for every layer index li2 strictly greater than li, down to n-1, since rows render top-to-bottom from the HIGHEST layer index. Returns 0 for the topmost-rendered layer (the one with the highest index).
frameGridTotalRowsHeight (4406-4409): sums frameGridRowHeight(i) over every layer index 0..n-1 — the grid's total content height given the current per-layer heights.

layerIndexAtGridY (4415-4425, preceded by a four-line comment at 4410-4414 framing it as the reverse of visualTopOfLayer and noting it replaces `state.layers.length-1-Math.floor(yRel/ROW_H)`): clamps yRel to >=0; walks layer indices from n-1 down to 0 (via `p` from 0..n-1, `li=n-1-p`), accumulating each layer's frameGridRowHeight until the running total would exceed y, returning that li; returns 0 if state.layers.length is 0 or if the loop falls through (walked every layer without y landing inside any row's span — the fallback the comment describes as identical to the old formula whenever every row is still plain ROW_H tall).

behavior: Guards on `#frame-grid` existing (4427-4428, returns undefined if missing).

Removes every existing `.tw-curve-strip` element first (4429-4430), unconditionally, before checking the toggle — so turning the feature off (state.showTweenCurves falsy, checked at 4431) still cleans up any strips left over from when it was on, then returns.

Iterates every `.frow` element in the grid (4432-4433, `grid.querySelectorAll('.frow')` then `.forEach`, a live DOM query against whatever renderTimeline already built for this frame). For each row, reads its first `.fc` cell's `dataset.layer` to recover the layer index `li` (4434-4437, skipping the row entirely if the cell/dataset is missing or li is NaN or state.layers[li] doesn't exist).
Calls layerTweenSpans(li) (4438, this scope's previous packet); skips the row if there are no spans (4439).

Creates one `.tw-curve-strip` wrapper div per qualifying row (4440-4442): absolutely positioned at left:0/bottom:0, width = state.totalFrames*FC, height = TWEEN_ROW_EXTRA_H, translucent dark background, sets the row's own `position:relative` (4443) so the absolutely-positioned strip anchors to it, and appends the wrapper to the row (4444).

For each span [fA,fB] (4445-4459): computes x0=fA*FC, w=(fB-fA)*FC; creates a `.tw-curve-strip-box` div absolutely positioned at that x/width spanning the wrapper's full height with a right border separating spans; sets pad=6 (4451); builds the actual curve editor via `buildTweenCurveSVG(li,fA,fB,Math.max(20,w-2*pad),TWEEN_ROW_EXTRA_H-2*pad)` (4455, this scope's next-packet function — the same builder the floating popup uses, per the in-source comment at 4452-4454) and absolutely positions the returned svg at (pad,pad) inside the box; appends the svg to the box (4457) and the box to the wrapper (4458).

packets.responsibility: The single implementation of the draggable-control-point easing-curve editor surface, shared byte-for-byte by both the persistent inline strips (previous packet) and the floating popup (next packet) so the drag/redraw/regenerate logic can never drift between the two call sites (CLAUDE.md §3). behavior: Section header (4463) plus a long lead-in comment (4464-4470) states the sharing rationale and that both call sites read/write the same state.tweenEasing entry, keeping inline and popup edits always in agreement.

Setup (4471-4479): computes `key=tweenSpanKey(li,fA,fB)` (tweens.js-owned, called not defined here); lazily creates `state.tweenEasing={}` if absent (4474) and `seg=state.tweenEasing[key]=state.tweenEasing[key]||{}` (4474, a write into document state on first access for any given pair); if `seg.points` is empty/missing, seeds it (4475-4479) from whatever curve is CURRENTLY effective globally (`window._curveEditor.getState().points`, read-only call into ui.js) falling back to a hardcoded default cubic-bezier-style four-point array `[{0,0},{.42,0},{.58,1},{1,1}]` when no global editor state exists yet — explicitly NOT a hardcoded default when a global curve does exist, per the in-source comment.
SVG scaffold (4480-4483): creates an `<svg>` in the SVG namespace sized svgW x svgH with `cursor:crosshair;touch-action:none`.

Coordinate mapping (4486-4504, with a 13-line comment at 4488-4500 explaining a 2026 fix, feedback #99): `toSX`/`toSY` map the logical [0,1] x domain and an OVERSHOOT-aware [Y_LO=-0.3, Y_HI=1.3] y domain (Y_SPAN=1.6) onto pixel space with a 6px inner pad on every side; `fromSX`/`fromSY` are the inverse, used to interpret pointer positions during drag, with `fromSY` clamping to the same [-0.3,1.3] range so back/elastic-style overshoot curves (routinely placing a point above y=1 or below y=0) always have a reachable on-screen handle at every SVG width/height, fixing a previously genuinely off-canvas point position rather than merely a cramped one.

redraw() (4506-4565): clears all SVG children; draws two dashed reference lines at y=0 and y=1 (the domain's 'neutral' bounds, not the SVG's own edges since Y_LO/Y_HI extend past them); samples the curve at 49 points (N=48) via `window._curveEditor.evalPointsCurve(pts,t)` (falls back to the identity `t` if the global evaluator is absent) and draws it as a single blue polyline; then, for each control point (loop from 4521), draws a draggable white/blue circle (r=5.5) wired with two listeners: `pointerdown` (4526-4558) captures the pointer ON THE SVG ELEMENT ITSELF rather than the circle (a 2026 fix, feedback #124, documented in an 11-line comment at 4528-4538, because redraw() destroys and recreates every circle on each move, and re-capturing a freshly created element mid-drag is unreliable across browsers), calls `pushUndo()` once per gesture if available (4546, with a comment at 4540-4545 noting this closes a bug where state.tweenEasing was written with no undo snapshot), then defines `move` (4547-4553, clamps the dragged point's x between its neighbors' x +/-0.001, or pins to exactly 0/1 for the first/last point; writes `p.x`/`p.y` directly onto the live `seg.points` array element at 4552, calls redraw() and scheduleRegen()) and `up` (4556, releases pointer capture, detaches both listeners, calls regenNow() so the FINAL position is always applied even if the debounce below hasn't fired) — both installed as SVG-level pointermove/pointerup listeners inside the pointerdown handler (4557), self-removing on `up`; and `dblclick` (4559-4562) removes the point (pts.splice at 4561) when it is neither the first nor last point and at least 3 points remain, then redraws and regenerates immediately.

Debounced regeneration (4566-4574, with a six-line comment at 4566-4571 explaining the tradeoff): `scheduleRegen` (4573) clears any pending timer and sets a new 120ms one calling `regenNow`; `regenNow` (4574) clears the timer and calls `onTweenPairCurveChanged(li,fA)` (next packet) — so continuous dragging redraws the curve every pointermove but only re-triggers the expensive tween regeneration once per 120ms of stillness, with `up`'s own regenNow() call guaranteeing the last position is never lost to a pending debounce.

Click-to-insert-point handler (4575-4583): attached directly to the svg element; ignored if the click target isn't the svg itself (i.e. a click on an existing circle doesn't also insert a new point); otherwise computes the clicked point's logical (nx,ny) via fromSX/fromSY, finds the correct sorted insertion index by x (first existing point whose x exceeds nx, or the end), inserts the new point via `pts.splice(idx,0,{x:nx,y:ny})` (4581), then redraws and regenerates immediately (4582, no debounce for insertion).
Initial `redraw()` call (4584) before returning `{svg, redraw, seg}` (4585) so the curve is drawn once synchronously before any interaction.
